label: early input steps after a leading e, plus last copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps) and does not reduce to one rule. It never fires at t=0,1 and rarely fires at the delimiter. There are two main components. (A) Copy phase, recall_idx==2, mostly in short sequences: rate is 52% for L=3 (the final output step) and lower for L=4. All of the top activations (0.9-1.0 of max) are in this component, usually when the step outputs e (the input there is orig(1)). (B) Original phase, t=2 or 3, when the first token is e (precision ~49%; a weaker version holds when the first token is y). Together these cover ~53% of activation mass at dev F1 0.42. The remaining activations are spread thinly over mid-sequence copy steps (recall_idx 3-5) and original steps where e/y appeared two tokens back (prev2_tok e has 7.6x lift). Letters u/r and digit 2 as input are mildly enriched.
